blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules so the function reads without the plan. A reader of the existing-account branch stumbles at `if account.plan != row.plan`, five levels deep: it reads as "update the plan", yet the plan is never written — it only gates whether new seats are added, so an existing account whose plan is unchanged silently gets none of the CSV's new seats; nothing says whether that is intended. The other filters are unexplained too: rows with an empty email are skipped without a word (`if !row.email.is_empty()`), and `seat.contains('@')` is an undocumented "a seat is an email address" check, duplicated in both branches together with the `db.add_seat` / `created += 1` loop. Simpler version: `continue` early on an empty email; resolve the account into `(id, existing_seats)` (creating it when absent); extract one helper such as `add_missing_seats(db, account_id, existing, &row.seats) -> Result<usize, DbError>` that filters with a named predicate (`is_seat_email`) and returns the count; and give the plan-difference condition a name or a comment that states why seats are only added when the plan differs.
findings.title: `import` hides its rules in five levels of nesting and a duplicated seat loop
